Selected Work

Automated Floor Plan Coloring

Anonymized Engineering Case · Local or Edge Deployment · Measured benchmark

Recognize rooms, apply materials and add labels on the user's machine, then export floor plans in batches.

Discuss a similar project Technical diagram

Industry problem and engineering challenge

Coloring areas, applying materials and annotating floor areas involve repetitive drafting work. Source drawings vary by format, boundary quality and furniture symbols. Drafters need a way to inspect recognition and correct errors.

Technical approach and architecture

Implementation and deliverables

Room geometry and drawing elements are recognized before local visual rules are applied floor by floor.

Outcome

Floor plans are processed locally with interactive color changes and multi-floor batch output.

  • Local drawing pipeline
  • Materials and annotation rules
  • Batch-output plans

Validation and evidence

Acceptance can start with compatibility and output checks on public samples, then measure latency on the actual device. The historical timing covers cached recomposition only.

Public evidence classification · Measured benchmark

Historical recoloring recomposition on a cache hit · Measured
≈0.4 s · Apply the colors using the existing cached floor-plan analysis. The timing excludes source analysis, file I/O and the complete interaction. Hardware and repetition count were not published.
